title: Insider IP theft: share collection -> encrypted-archive staging -> USB exfil (Windows)

alert.summary: DLP alert: after-hours bulk copy of engineering design files to a removable USB drive on ENG-WS-22 by d.coleman.
alert.source: DLP removable-media monitor + Sysmon process telemetry

decoy_hypothesis.statement: H1: This is an external intrusion - a brute-force from {bf_ip} broke in and the backup agent's outbound HTTPS to 52.95.110.10 is the attacker exfiltrating the design files to the cloud.

corrected_hypothesis.statement: H2: This is an insider data-theft, not an external breach. The engineer d.coleman, using valid credentials after hours, robocopied the IP_Designs share, packed it into a password-protected 7-Zip archive, and copied the archive plus raw CAD/firmware files to a personal SanDisk USB drive (E:). The brute-force never succeeded and the cloud-backup egress is the sanctioned corporate backup agent.
corrected_hypothesis.rationale_suffix: All collection and exfil is by valid d.coleman credentials to a USB drive; the brute-force is benign scanner noise and 52.95.110.10 is the approved backup endpoint.

refutation.no_success_reason: every logon from {bf_ip} is a 4625 failure - the external scanner never authenticated, so this is not an external breach
refutation.benign_reason: threat intel rates {bf_ip} benign ({ti_note}); the cloud egress is the sanctioned backup agent

containment: Preserve ENG-WS-22 and image the SanDisk USB (serial 4C530001110523117025) under legal hold.
Disable d.coleman's accounts and revoke access pending HR/legal investigation.
Block USB mass-storage write via GPO on engineering endpoints.
Quantify exfiltrated IP from the staging archive (designs.zip) and the raw files copied to E:.
Review ENG-FS-01 IP_Designs share access logs for the full scope of collection.
Do NOT chase the benign brute-force or the sanctioned backup egress - they are not the incident.
